Subject: Finishing notes from Northforge call (deployment needs + econ)

Team — quick recap from my 2:30p with James (CTO) and Leah (product). High level: they liked Redwood's latency profile, care deeply about predictable unit economics and network isolation. Key items to feed into pricing/capacity proposals: 

- Workload: primarily chat + search reranking. Estimated monthly tokens: ~1.2B tokens (generation + input). Expected peak concurrency ~250–350 req/s during US business hours. Typical prompt + response average seq length ~120 tokens inbound + 280 tokens outbound (they'll confirm).
- Security/regulatory: SOC 2 required, VPC peering preferred. They have PII in prompts — want data-at-rest controls and customer-managed KMS if we go private.
- Pilot ask: 6–8 week pilot to validate latency and cost. They prefer to start in hosted API for speed but want an option path to Dedicated or Private after pilot if economics justify.
- Procurement: finance@northforge.com will own PO. James asked for a simple financing picture comparing: (A) hosted per-token with estimated monthly spend, (B) Dedicated reserved commit sizing + monthly fee, and (C) Private (VPC) onboarding + TCO (monthly infra + support).

Action items for us: 
1) Priyom — can you produce two capacity scenarios (concurrency/instance counts) mapping to the token assumptions (1.2B/mo) so we can show a Dedicated reserved commit $/month and a corresponding latency SLO? Also list any observable perf delta vs hosted.
2) Marissa — draft three commercial options (pilot hosted credits, 3-month reserved pilot, private onboarding estimate) and include typical contract/legal bullets and provisioning lead times.
3) I'll capture the ask to finance and loop James once we have numbers; attach quick pricing summary for context.

Attachment: redwood_pricing_summary_v2.pdf (one-pager with baseline per-token and capacity assumptions).

Thanks —
Logan Wright

Thanks for the recap — I sketched two concrete scenarios to attach to Marissa's commercial options. High-level assumptions below; I'll produce a short spreadsheet with line items tomorrow.

Scenario A — Hosted (per-token estimate)
- Assumptions: 1.2B tokens / month (mixed inbound+outbound), average seq length 400 tokens per request.
- Estimated egress: ~480M generated tokens per month.
- Rough price estimate (demo numbers): $0.00065 per generated token -> ~ $312k/month. Banding/discounts can reduce this materially.
- Pros: fastest to start, no infra onboarding, Redwood handles infra ops. Cons: less isolation, potential variability in unit cost at scale.

Scenario B — Dedicated reserved commit
- Sizing: for peak concurrency ~300 req/s with avg latency SLO <300ms, we'd recommend a dedicated pool of 8 x A100-equivalent workers (quantized model execution), plus 2 controller nodes for HA.
- Committed monthly price (example): $65k/month reserved (includes infra + orchestration + support). Burst capacity billed overage similarly or via short-term burst buffer. Equivalent per-token unit cost in this sizing comes down to ~$0.00018–0.00023 (depends on effective utilization).
- Pros: predictable monthly cost, stronger isolation, reduced per-token spend at scale. Cons: lead time to provision, minimum commit term typically 3–6 months.

Questions for Northforge to finalize numbers:
- Can James/Leah confirm average tokens per request and % of requests that are long-form generation vs short prompt completions?
- Do they need guaranteed region placement (us-east vs us-west) or are multi-region acceptable?

I will attach the capacity worksheet (I'll upload the spreadsheet to the deal record) and highlight the assumptions so finance can double-check.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions Architect

Hi James — looping in the items Logan and Priyom discussed and putting three commercial paths on paper so your procurement/finance team has clear options. Priyom's capacity notes are included below for context.

Option 1 — Hosted pilot (fastest start)- Term: 8-week pilot- Commercial: $5,000 in API credits + standard per-token pricing during pilot- Objective: validate latency, integration, and initial cost run-rate- Onboarding: 2 business days

Option 2 — Dedicated reserved pilot (recommended if you want predictability)- Term: 3 months reserved (pilot)- Commitment example: $65k/month (sample sizing aligned to 300 req/s peaks)- Includes: dedicated GPU pool, priority support, canary rollout window, and a migration credit if you convert to a longer-term commit- Onboarding: 10–14 business days

Option 3 — Private VPC / on-prem (compliance-first)- Term: TCO model with onboarding fee- Example pricing: $150k/month + one-time onboarding & professional services fee (varies by network & KMS integration)- Includes: customer-managed KMS integration, audit log retention, and private control plane options- Onboarding: 4–8 weeks (depends on legal/network)

Commercial notes:
- We can offer a step-down commercial: pilot credits apply to first invoice if converted to a committed reserved deal within 45 days.
- We typically require a PO for reserved pilots; finance@northforge.com is the contact we would invoice.

Attached: northforge_pilot_sow_draft.docx (hit points and timeline).

2) Provide procurement contact and any internal timeline constraints.
3) Book a technical workshop (Priyom suggested a 90-min deep dive) — how does Oct 14 or Oct 15 look?
